entries: Sunrise is at 6:58 AM with 11 h 9 m of daylight. Overnight at North Island, rain from 7:52 PM to 9:52 PM, 0.15 in (3.8 mm); air 68–73 °F (20–23 °C) and humidity 73–87%, 68 °F (20 °C) and 73% at 5:52 AM. Water 75 °F (23.8 °C) at CDIP 191.

CDIP 191 at 5:00 AM: 14.3 s from S 182°, 2.8 ft (0.84 m); 9.9 s from W 280°, 2.3 ft (0.71 m); wind sea 4.2 s from W 277°, 1.8 ft (0.54 m). At 11:00 AM yesterday: 12.5 s from W 270°, 3.4 ft (1.03 m); 13.3 s from S 186°, 3.3 ft (1.00 m). Breaking at 5:00 AM, against 11:00 AM yesterday: North 3.3 ft (0.99 m), fading from 4.1 ft (1.26 m); Center 3.1 ft (0.94 m), fading from 4.4 ft (1.34 m); South 3.3 ft (1.00 m), little change.

The tide is pushing to 6.4 ft (1.97 m) at 7:31 AM then dropping to 2.8 ft (0.85 m) at 1:33 PM. The previous AM low was 2.1 ft (0.63 m) at 1:08 AM and the PM high will be 6.2 ft (1.90 m) at 7:26 PM. The gauge is running 1.5 ft (0.46 m) over the harmonic prediction, over the last 3 days. Today's range is 4.4 ft (1.34 m), building toward springs; springs around Oct 25. On the 2016 survey the tide moves where the waves break, not how big they are; this season's sandbars are not known.

W 270° at 8 mph (7 kt) at 5:52 AM: cross-shore at North; onshore at Center and South. At this hour on the 31 days before: North cross-shore on 3, light or variable on 13; Center onshore on 2, light or variable on 13; South onshore on 2, light or variable on 13. Median 5 mph (4 kt).

Former hurricane [Trudy](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/2026/TRUDY_graphics.php): every fix NHC has logged or forecast is behind land from Point Loma South, so nothing it has sent reaches the breaks.
